Concept role: dwp:Applicability.","text":"DMG 77035 distinguishes new claims from 15 May 2019 and continuity protection linked to Pension Credit or pension-age Housing Benefit on 14 May 2019. DMG 77140–77184 distinguish the mixed-age definition, Universal Credit interaction, excluded-partner exceptions and effective dates. The general exclusion is not the complete rule. DMG memo 04/24 paragraphs 15–17 add a protected mixed-age migration route from 8 June 2024: the specified protected couples sent a migration notice may reclaim pension-age Housing Benefit or claim Pension Credit within three months after the relevant UC or HB award ends. That route requires its stated prior entitlement and migration facts; it is not a general right for every mixed-age couple. Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.","text":"Claimants who have no partner (including self- funders)
78088 An additional amount for the severely disabled is applicable to a person who is permanently in a

care home if all the conditions are satisfied1.


Note: This will normally be self funding claimants, but DMs should be aware that it will also include
residents where the payment of “AA” or DLA/PiP continues for the first four weeks after admission.


                                                                   1 SPC Regs, reg 5(1)(b) & Sch I, para 1(1)(a)


Example


Shafaq has no partner and lives at home with his sisters. He is in receipt of the care component of DLA at
the middle rate and no one receives CA, or UC that includes the carer element for caring for him. The
conditions for the award of an additional amount for the disabled are not satisfied. Shafaq goes into a
care home on a permanent basis. The DM decides that Shafaq is entitled to an additional amount for the
disabled at the lower rate from the date that he moves into the care home. This is because


1. he is in receipt of the care component of DLA at the middle rate and


2. the other residents of the home do not normally reside with him and


3. no one is in receipt of CA, or UC that includes the carer element, for caring for him.


Entitlement to the additional amount continues as long as all of the above are satisfied.

Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.","text":"Temporary residence in a care home

Claimants who have no partner
78084 An additional amount for the severely disabled may not be applicable if a claimant who has no

partner does not normally live alone1. Such a claimant will not satisfy the conditions for this additional
amount while they are temporarily in a care home (see DMG 77007). This is because their stay is
temporary and they continue to normally reside at home.


                                                                                  1 SPC Regs, Sch I, para 1(1)


Example


Nasreen has no partner and lives with her son. The conditions for the award of an additional amount for
the disabled are not satisfied. Nasreen goes into a care home temporarily. An additional amount for the
severely disabled is not applicable because she continues to normally reside at home with her son.

Concept role: dwp:Applicability.","text":"A limited disregard for the residence condition of the Pension Credit severe-disability additional amount, not a finding that a person is absent from the household for every purpose. Assess normal residence separately. The captured DMG 78077 categories are: a person aged under 18; a person receiving source-defined “AA”, highest- or middle-rate DLA care, standard- or enhanced-rate PIP or ADP daily living, or AFIP; a person certified as blind or severely sight impaired by a consultant ophthalmologist or treated as such; a person living with the claimant to care for the claimant or partner who is engaged by a charitable or voluntary organisation which charges the claimant or partner for their services; that carer’s partner; and a source-defined qualifying young person, or a child for Child Benefit purposes. DMG 78008 limits treated blindness to 28 weeks after regained eyesight and no longer being certified. A voluntary organisation is non-profit and is not a public authority or local authority. Named young-person definitions have age, education, training, benefit-receipt and interruption conditions; neither education alone nor being under 20 is enough. DMG 78078(1) requires first joining the household to care for the claimant or partner, with the claimant or partner satisfying the additional-amount conditions immediately beforehand, and applies only for the first 12 weeks after joining. Its commercial-payment route concerns a person who is not a close relative: payment liability runs either from that person to the claimant or partner for occupation of their dwelling, or from the claimant or partner to that person for occupation of that person’s dwelling; it also covers membership of that person’s household. DMG 78079 requires legal liability and a payment broadly comparable to a lodger’s similar accommodation and facilities. The joint-occupation route requires co-ownership or joint liability to the same landlord, with its non-close-relative condition and the person’s-partner branch. The close-relative exception requires satisfying DMG 78078(3) or (4) as well as the timing condition: the claimant or partner’s co-ownership or joint liability must have arisen before 11 April 1988 or, if later, on or before first occupation; the note uses the right-to-occupy date, not a later moving-in date. Close relative has the captured legal, adoptive and half-sibling meanings. DMG 78080’s registered shared-lives route must retain the accommodation/support and commercial licence conditions and the exclusion where other people cannot be ignored; its completed example is not a general award rule or a current rate. Memo 02/25 paragraph 15 adds Pension Age Disability Payment to the ignored-person benefit list from 21 October 2024, separately from the memo’s claimant/partner and housing-deduction propositions. The dated statutory paragraph 2 also contains Scottish Adult Disability Living Allowance wording requiring separate legal reconciliation; this concept does not consolidate it. Receipt conditions need the full DMG 78060 continuation: its partner-patient item must not be transferred automatically to a third person. Residence, receipt and component, age, care arrangements, relationship, liability and relevant dates remain unknown until evidenced. Source text is not current-law assurance and proposed meaning is not an official interpretation. Concept role: dwp:Guidance.","text":"The captured chapter must be read with its amendment memoranda. DMG memo 02/25 paragraphs 13–16 add Pension Age Disability Payment (PADP) from 21 October 2024 to the AA meaning and qualifying/ignored-person provisions. DMG memo 06/25 paragraphs 30–33 add Scottish Adult Disability Living Allowance (SADLA) to specified Pension Credit disability and housing-cost provisions; its introduction gives commencement as 21 March 2025. DMG memo 01/26 paragraphs 5–7 amend Carer Support Payment (CSP) terminology and the specified bereavement run-on from 15 March 2026.
